proposals.label: Global Digital Compact narrowing the divide
proposals.definition: Demand that the Pact for the Future and Global Digital Compact focus on narrowing the digital divide.
proposals.inclusion: Include calls to narrow the digital divide in connection with AI or UN digital agreements.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude divide statements unrelated to technology.
proposals.boundary_cases: Reference to the Global Digital Compact also qualifies for AI_UN_ROLE if the UN process is the focus.

examples.quote: The implementation of the Pact of the Future and the Global Digital Compact must focus on narrowing the digital divide.

proposals.label: AI access for developing countries
proposals.definition: Demand that developing countries gain access to safe and secure digital technology including AI, rather than technology being reserved for a select few.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages demanding developing-country access to AI or objecting to technology being exclusive to a few.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude climate-finance-only demands.
proposals.boundary_cases: Technology transfer demands from developed countries could also fit AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING.

examples.quote: Technology and innovation should not be exclusively for the select few.
Access to safe and secure digital technology for developing countries, including artificial intelligence, is crucial for future sustainable growth.

proposals.label: Developed-country responsibility for technology transfer
proposals.definition: Call on developed countries to fulfil obligations including transfer of technology to developing countries.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages demanding technology transfer or support from developed countries in the context of AI/digital technology.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages focused only on access inequality without a support demand.
proposals.boundary_cases: If technology transfer is framed only for climate, code only when AI/digital is in the same argument.

examples.quote: We also need developed countries to fulfil their responsibility, including on climate financing, green investment and the transfer of technology.

proposals.label: Technology's promise and risk
proposals.definition: AI and digital innovation framed as accelerating development while their misuse deepens inequality, insecurity and crime.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages explicitly pairing AI's development promise with risks of misuse.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages discussing only crime enforcement without AI framing.
proposals.boundary_cases: If the risk emphasized is crime, also code AI_CYBER_SECURITY.

examples.quote: Technology illustrate both the promise and the risk.
Artificial intelligence and digital innovation can accelerate development and expand opportunities

proposals.label: Misuse enabling transnational online crime
proposals.definition: Misuse of AI and digital tech linked to transnational crime such as online scams, requiring international cooperation against criminal networks.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages linking AI/digital misuse to transnational crime, scams or insecurity.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude military uses of AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: Anti-scam enforcement passages without any AI/technology link should not be coded.

examples.quote: their misuse can also deepen inequality, insecurity, and transnational crime

proposals.label: Hiroshima AI Process and trustworthy AI rules
proposals.definition: The speaker promotes international governance of AI, especially its own Hiroshima AI Process principles and code of conduct for safe, secure and trustworthy (generative) AI.
proposals.inclusion: Include references to international AI principles, codes of conduct, or governance initiatives such as the Hiroshima AI Process.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude purely domestic digital policy without international rule-making.
proposals.boundary_cases: Commitment to contribute to AI discussions at the UN also qualifies for AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: Japan took the initiative to launch the Hiroshima AI Process, establishing the world's first international world's first international principles and code of conduct to govern generative AI.
there is an urgent need to establish international governance on artificial intelligence (AI) in order to maximize the opportunities brought by AI while mitigating its risks

proposals.label: Safety cooperation on frontier AI
proposals.definition: Cooperation on AI safety to respond to risks of highly capable frontier AI, including hosting AI summits for this purpose.
proposals.inclusion: Include references to frontier AI risks, AI safety cooperation, or safety institutes/summits.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude generic 'safe, secure and trustworthy' slogans without a frontier/safety-risk element (AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE).
proposals.boundary_cases: 'Safe, secure and trustworthy AI ecosystem' combined with frontier-risk cooperation is coded here.

examples.quote: will enhance cooperation on safety to respond to the risks of highly capable frontier AI

proposals.label: AI's tremendous opportunities and challenges
proposals.definition: AI framed as bringing tremendous opportunities alongside risks, including national security challenges.
proposals.inclusion: Include explicit statements pairing AI benefits with AI risks or challenges.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude risk-only statements.
proposals.boundary_cases: If the national-security challenge is elaborated as military use, also code AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS.

examples.quote: While advances in AI bring tremendous opportunities for humanity, they also pose challenges, including those related to national security.

proposals.label: Digitalization balanced with human dignity
proposals.definition: Balancing digitalization and AI with human dignity, privacy and human rights through compatible international rules.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages linking AI or digital rules to privacy, human rights, or dignity.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude digitalization support to developing countries without rights framing.
proposals.boundary_cases: Generic digitalization risks count only when AI is referenced in the same argument, as here via the Hiroshima AI Process.

examples.quote: there are risks of privacy and human rights violations. We need a digital ecosystem and international rules that are compatible with human dignity.

proposals.label: Tackling non-factual information and propaganda
proposals.definition: Urgent measures against the spread of information not based on facts and propaganda, raised in the context of AI and technological innovation.
proposals.inclusion: Include mentions of disinformation or propaganda raised alongside AI challenges.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude disinformation discussions with no technology context.
proposals.boundary_cases: When disinformation is mentioned adjacent to AI but not explicitly caused by AI, code with lower confidence.

examples.quote: We also urgently need measures to tackle the spread of information not based on facts, as well as the spread of propaganda.

proposals.label: Contributing to UN AI discussions
proposals.definition: Commitment to contribute to AI discussions at the United Nations.
proposals.inclusion: Include explicit commitments to UN AI deliberations or processes.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude general UN reform discussion without AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: Calls for the UN to build 'new rules' generally, adjacent to AI, are borderline.

examples.quote: We will continue to actively contribute to the discussions on AI at the United Nations.

proposals.label: AI universal basic society for all
proposals.definition: Vision that everyone and every country should share in the basic benefits of AI, framed as an 'AI universal basic society' or 'AI for all' tied to rights and leaving no one behind.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages proposing universal access to AI benefits as a social or rights-based goal (e.g. AI universal basic health, AI for all).
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages that only describe access gaps for developing countries without a universal-benefit vision; code those AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.
proposals.boundary_cases: Global AI hub platforms offered to share this vision fit here and may also fit AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING.

examples.quote: It is the AI universal basic society where everyone can benefit from technological progress.
a global AI universal basic society where no country or individual is left out from access to the basic benefits of AI development

proposals.label: Leading global AI norms and summits
proposals.definition: Speaker's country positions itself as leading international AI norm-setting through summits, declarations, forums and proposed international organizations.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages on hosting AI summits/forums, adopting declarations (e.g. Seoul Declaration) or proposing international rule-making bodies for AI or digital ethics.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude purely domestic AI programmes without international norm-setting.
proposals.boundary_cases: Proposals for a UN-based organization fit here and AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: The Seoul Declaration for safe, innovative and inclusive AI, adopted at the AI Seoul Summit in May, marked a significant milestone in building the norms for civilian AI.
Korean Government plans to host a global AI forum.

proposals.label: Collaboration with UN AI bodies
proposals.definition: Engagement with UN AI processes: SG high-level advisory body, Security Council open debate, proposed UN organization on digital ethics.
proposals.inclusion: Include explicit references to UN AI bodies or using UN fora for AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude non-UN summits (APEC, AI Seoul Summit) unless a UN link is made.
proposals.boundary_cases: Presiding over a UNSC debate on AI counts here.

examples.quote: collaborate closely with the high-level advisory body on AI being established by the United Nations
I have also proposed the establishment of an international organization under the United Nations to discuss and set forth rules regarding digital ethics.

proposals.label: Norms for military use of AI
proposals.definition: References to responsible AI in the military domain and AI as a security capability.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages on REAIM, military AI norms, or AI as critical to security capabilities.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude civilian AI safety and cyber crime passages without military framing.
proposals.boundary_cases: AI as critical to 'security capabilities' alongside cyber attacks may also be AI_CYBER_SECURITY.

examples.quote: further laid the groundwork for norms for the military use of AI
In an era where artificial intelligence technology is critical to security capabilities and cyber attacks threaten national security

proposals.label: AI revolution as opportunity and crisis
proposals.definition: AI explicitly framed as both opportunity and crisis, with outcomes (dystopia vs prosperity) depending on proactive response.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages contrasting AI-driven prosperity with inequality, dystopia or rights abuses.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude one-sided optimistic or pessimistic mentions.
proposals.boundary_cases: Youth employment anxiety within such framing also fits AI_ECONOMY_LABOR.

examples.quote: The artificial intelligence revolution is both a massive opportunity and a crisis for humanity.
If we passively let ourselves be dragged along by the changes of the AI era, we will meet a dystopia of deepening polarization and inequality

proposals.label: AI-driven fake news threatening democracy
proposals.definition: Misuse of AI spreading fake news that endangers freedom and liberal democracy.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages linking AI misuse to fake news or threats to democratic order.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude generic rights risk statements without information-integrity content.
proposals.boundary_cases: A digital bill of rights proposal may also be coded AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS.

examples.quote: If we fail to curb the spread of fake news resulting from the misuse of AI and digital technologies, our freedom will be at risk

proposals.label: AI risks to human rights and dignity
proposals.definition: AI framed in terms of human rights and dignity, both as a risk and as a means to realize rights.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages on AI risks to human rights/dignity, digital ethics rules, or AI to realize economic and social rights.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages about access alone without rights language.
proposals.boundary_cases: AI 'accelerating realization of economic, social and cultural rights' counts here and in AI_UNIVERSAL_BASIC_SOCIETY.

examples.quote: also poses potential risks to human rights and dignity

proposals.label: Great opportunities, risk of sinister misuse
proposals.definition: AI and cutting-edge technologies framed as transforming human life with great opportunities but also risks of misuse for sinister purposes.
proposals.inclusion: Include brief statements pairing AI's transformative opportunities with misuse risks.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages specifying concrete military AI or governance proposals.
proposals.boundary_cases: A generic duality statement followed by a call for a strengthened UN stays here unless specific AI governance is proposed.

examples.quote: Artificial intelligence and other new cutting-edge technology are transforming every domain of human life, offering great opportunities, but at the same time, they also carry risks of being misused for sinister purposes.

proposals.label: Widening AI gap for developing nations
proposals.definition: The AI gap between states, beyond the digital gap, that prevents developing countries from using AI for development due to inadequate infrastructure.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages describing an AI or digital divide limiting developing countries' use of AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude requests for assistance with no description of the gap (AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING).
proposals.boundary_cases: Passages that both describe the divide and request technology transfer are coded here and AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING.

examples.quote: An even greater gap is being created in relation to artificial intelligence.

proposals.label: Technology transfer and technical assistance
proposals.definition: Calls for technology transfer, capacity-building and technical assistance so developing countries can leverage AI and digital tools.
proposals.inclusion: Include explicit requests for technology transfers, capacity-building or technical assistance related to AI/digital technologies.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude general development finance requests unrelated to technology.
proposals.boundary_cases: Calls to 'bridge the digital divide' with assistance count here and AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: promote meaningful technology transfers, ensure equitable access for developing nations, bridge the digital divide
we call for increased capacity-building and technical assistance to bridge the global digital divide

proposals.label: AI accelerating sustainable development
proposals.definition: AI presented as an opportunity to accelerate sustainable development and growth.
proposals.inclusion: Include statements that AI offers opportunities for sustainable development or is a development tool.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages only about gaps without development benefits.
proposals.boundary_cases: 'Using AI as a development tool' within a divide passage can be coded both.

examples.quote: Digital technologies and artificial intelligence offer unprecedented opportunities to accelerate sustainable development.

proposals.label: Ethical guidelines and international law compliance
proposals.definition: Responsible, ethical AI consistent with international law and IHL, including national AI ethical guidelines and humanity's interests.
proposals.inclusion: Include references to AI ethical guidelines, responsible use, and compliance with international (humanitarian) law.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude calls for regulation that do not reference ethics or law principles.
proposals.boundary_cases: IHL references imply military uses; code AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS only if weapons/warfare are explicit.

examples.quote: We have developed national AI ethical guidelines in line with international frameworks.
The interest of humanity must always guide the development and use of these technologies.

proposals.label: Urgent regulatory regime for AI
proposals.definition: Calls to address the absence of a regulatory or supervisory regime for AI and new technologies in cyberspace.
proposals.inclusion: Include calls for regulation or supervisory regimes for AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude national regulations described as achievements (AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY).
proposals.boundary_cases: Partnership-based cybersecurity approaches without AI regulation go to AI_CYBER_SECURITY.

examples.quote: The absence of a regulatory supervisory regime concerning the use of new technologies in cyberspace and in artificial intelligence needs to be addressed urgently.

proposals.label: AI spreading disinformation and disruption
proposals.definition: Concern that AI and cyber technologies spread disinformation and undermine established scientific findings.
proposals.inclusion: Include mentions of AI-enabled disinformation or undermining facts.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude cyberattacks on infrastructure without information content.
proposals.boundary_cases: 'Large-scale disruption' alone goes to AI_CYBER_SECURITY.

examples.quote: spread disinformation and undermine scientifically established findings

proposals.label: Proposal for neutral sovereign AI zone
proposals.definition: A specific proposal to the Assembly to establish a neutral sovereign artificial intelligence zone.
proposals.inclusion: Include proposals for neutral, sovereign or non-aligned AI zones or spaces.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude general data-sovereignty claims without an institutional proposal.
proposals.boundary_cases: If a proposal is framed mainly around independence from powerful states, also code AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION.

examples.quote: I present this August Assembly a proposal to set up a neutral sovereign artificial intelligence zone.

proposals.label: AI-powered disaster early warning
proposals.definition: Speaker describes a national system linking Earth observation, supercomputing and AI to predict floods and droughts, offered for global sharing under Early Warnings for All.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages on AI applied to climate hazard prediction, early warning or disaster resilience.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude early-warning passages that do not mention AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: Offers to share the AI solution internationally may also be coded AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING; the adjacent passage on global early-warning partnership without AI is context only.

examples.quote: we initiated the development of an advanced digital solution linking Earth observation with supercomputing and artificial intelligence

proposals.label: Sharing AI solutions and monitoring capacity
proposals.definition: Offer to share an AI-enabled hazard system with partners and call for a global partnership to address countries' lack of monitoring capacity.
proposals.inclusion: Include offers to share AI tools or build other countries' capacity through partnerships.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude purely domestic AI deployment without an international sharing element.
proposals.boundary_cases: The follow-on call for an early-warning partnership does not name AI and should be coded only in the context of the preceding AI passage.

examples.quote: We are ready to share that solution with our partners globally.
many countries lack the capacity to monitor all hazards and are restricted in their access

proposals.label: Human-centred AI grounded in rights and democracy
proposals.definition: AI and the digital future should follow a human-centred approach based on human rights, democracy and the rule of law.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages demanding human-centred or rights-based AI development.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages on digital governance that do not reference rights or human-centredness.
proposals.boundary_cases: Rights protection mentioned generally for digital technologies alongside AI counts here when AI is named in the same sentence or passage.

examples.quote: Our digital future and artificial intelligence should be guided by a humancentred approach based on human rights, democracy and the rule of law.

proposals.label: Global Digital Compact and multistakeholder governance
proposals.definition: Support for the Global Digital Compact and inclusive, multi-stakeholder global digital and AI governance oriented toward the SDGs.
proposals.inclusion: Include references to the Global Digital Compact or multi-stakeholder global governance of AI and digital technologies.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude national digital policies.
proposals.boundary_cases: Where AI is only one of several governed technologies (digital, space), code here if a global governance process is named; otherwise AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: The Global Digital Compact should harness the potential of digital technologies to accelerate the achievement of the SDGs.
Bulgaria supports inclusive, multi-stakeholder approaches to global digital governance, artificial intelligence, and space technologies

proposals.label: Global Digital Compact co-facilitation
proposals.definition: Speaker highlights role in co-facilitating the UN Global Digital Compact as the framework for digital and AI governance and closing divides.
proposals.inclusion: Passages referencing the Global Digital Compact or UN General Assembly processes on digital/AI governance.
proposals.exclusion: General cooperation calls without UN processes (use AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE).
proposals.boundary_cases: Compact commitments to close digital divides also take AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: to establish the governance required for a sustainable digital future, including with respect to artificial intelligence
Sweden is co-facilitating the process in the General Assembly of developing a global digital compact

proposals.label: Harness promise while mitigating risks
proposals.definition: AI framed as holding immense promise while entailing risks that must be addressed and mitigated.
proposals.inclusion: Passages urging support for AI innovation while addressing risks, or harnessing potential and mitigating risks.
proposals.exclusion: One-sided benefit statements.
proposals.boundary_cases: Mentions of security and human rights challenges alongside opportunities count here.

examples.quote: The global community must support innovation while addressing risks.
This fast-moving development also entails challenges for international security and human rights.

proposals.label: AI for climate, health and SDGs
proposals.definition: AI presented as a tool to accelerate climate action, global health and the SDGs, or address pressing common challenges.
proposals.inclusion: Passages linking AI to climate, health, SDGs or common global challenges.
proposals.exclusion: Economic jobs framing alone (use AI_ECONOMY_LABOR).
proposals.boundary_cases: Generic 'immense promise' statements count when tied to common challenges.

examples.quote: accelerate our efforts on climate change, global health and the Sustainable Development Goals
Emerging technologies such as AI hold immense promise in addressing some of our most pressing common challenges.

proposals.label: Closing digital divides
proposals.definition: Commitment to close digital divides among and within countries in the context of AI and digital governance.
proposals.inclusion: Passages about closing digital divides.
proposals.exclusion: Capacity programmes (use AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING).
proposals.boundary_cases: When framed only as a Compact commitment, also code AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: close digital divides among and within countries

proposals.label: Regulating AI to protect rights and freedoms
proposals.definition: AI and new technologies must be regulated democratically and aligned with human dignity, privacy, personal freedoms and democratic values.
proposals.inclusion: Passages calling for regulation of AI in the name of rights, privacy, dignity or freedom of conscience and expression.
proposals.exclusion: Calls for regulation framed around safety, military use or development without rights content.
proposals.boundary_cases: Calls for 'democratic regulation' of platforms and AI count here when tied to rights and dignity.

examples.quote: artificial intelligence and the data economy must, however, be better regulated and aligned with personal freedoms, respect for our private lives
Any technology must be used with one goal in mind — ensuring the dignity and rights of every individual.

proposals.label: Disruptive technology cuts both ways
proposals.definition: Recognition that AI and other disruptive technologies work for both good and bad, rejecting naive techno-optimism.
proposals.inclusion: Passages stating that AI and related technologies are not automatically a force for good and can cut both ways.
proposals.exclusion: Passages naming only harms.
proposals.boundary_cases: Statements that technology outpaces human adaptation lean here when benefits are also acknowledged.

examples.quote: We forgot that all disruptive technologies work in both directions, good and bad.

proposals.label: AI and platforms amplifying crises
proposals.definition: AI grouped with social media platforms as amplifiers of disinformation, hate speech and existing crises.
proposals.inclusion: Passages linking AI or platforms to disinformation or hate speech acting as accelerants of crises.
proposals.exclusion: Passages that discuss social media without AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: Where AI is only mentioned in a list with platforms, code here if the harm is information-related.

examples.quote: social media platforms, artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies can act like steroids on our current crises

proposals.label: AI for emissions reduction and climate
proposals.definition: AI applied to big data and IoT is framed as enabling emissions reduction, efficient logistics, renewables and circular economy.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages linking AI to climate mitigation or environmental efficiency.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude general digitalization-for-climate claims that do not name AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: If AI is only one item in a list of climate-helpful technologies without explanation, also code AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION.

examples.quote: Artificial intelligence applied to big data and the internet of things facilitate more efficient logistics and transportation, emissions reduction

proposals.label: Ethical, human-centred digital technologies including AI
proposals.definition: Development and use of digital technologies including AI must be ethical and human-centred, with rights protected online and offline.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages requiring ethical principles or human-centredness in AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages about digital access alone.
proposals.boundary_cases: Calls for UN digital cooperation in the same passage may also be coded AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: The development and use of Digital technologies, including Artificial Intelligence, based on ethical principles, must be human-centred.

proposals.label: COVID-19 accelerating AI and digital deployment
proposals.definition: AI is mentioned as part of a pandemic-accelerated digital revolution (with robotics, e-government, remote work), to be harnessed while mitigating negative impacts.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages tying AI deployment to COVID-19 or broad digital revolution alongside other digital tools.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude substantive AI-specific governance or risk discussion.
proposals.boundary_cases: This is close to AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION; code both when AI is merely listed.

examples.quote: COVID-19 has accelerated the deployment of artificial intelligence, robotics, digital payments, e-government services, and remote work.

proposals.label: Equitable investment to share AI benefits
proposals.definition: Calls for equitable investment in emerging technologies like AI so benefits are equally shared between high- and low-income countries.
proposals.inclusion: Passages urging equitable investment or sharing of AI benefits across income levels.
proposals.exclusion: General digital jobs statements without AI (generic digitalization).
proposals.boundary_cases: Investment calls with concrete programmes may also take AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING.

examples.quote: To ensure that the benefits are equally shared, we must continue to invest equitably in emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence.

proposals.label: Digital jobs addressing migration drivers
proposals.definition: Digital transformation and high-quality digital jobs framed as a practical response to drivers of irregular migration by closing human-capital gaps.
proposals.inclusion: Passages linking digital/AI jobs to economic opportunity and migration.
proposals.exclusion: Job displacement concerns (still this code but note framing).
proposals.boundary_cases: This is mostly generic digitalization; code only when AI is present in the same passage.

examples.quote: Highquality digital jobs are a practical response to the underlying drivers of irregular migration

proposals.label: Smart global governance of emerging technologies
proposals.definition: Call to urgently create global governance frameworks for science and emerging technologies such as AI, balancing benefits and prevention of threats.
proposals.inclusion: Include calls for global AI governance frameworks.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude mere references to adopted resolutions without a governance call.
proposals.boundary_cases: Welcoming the Global Digital Compact as a basis for governance is also AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: we should urgently create smart global governance frameworks with a long-term vision for science and technology, especially emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence

proposals.label: Welcoming UN AI resolutions and Compact
proposals.definition: Speakers welcome specific UN instruments on AI, such as the Global Digital Compact and General Assembly resolution 78/265 on safe, secure and trustworthy AI.
proposals.inclusion: Include references to UN AI resolutions, the Global Digital Compact or Summit of the Future outcomes on AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude governance calls that do not reference a UN instrument.
proposals.boundary_cases: Fragmentary passages citing a resolution number still count here.

examples.quote: States to ensure the reliability and security of artificial intelligence (resolution 78/265), in a significant step forward.
I welcome the documents adopted at the Summit for the Future, especially the Global Digital Compact

proposals.label: AI transforming education systems
proposals.definition: AI presented as changing how people learn and as a tool education systems can use for management, teaching and learning.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages on using AI in education systems or preparing education for AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude generic education statements without AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: Broad claims that AI changes how people work may additionally be coded AI_ECONOMY_LABOR.

examples.quote: Education systems could use artificial intelligence to change their management, teaching and learning.

proposals.label: AI transforming how societies live
proposals.definition: AI described as a rapid force transforming societies, including how people learn, work and live together.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages describing AI as broadly transforming society or daily life without specifying benefits or harms.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages focused on specific sectors only.
proposals.boundary_cases: If AI appears only in a list of trends, use AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION instead.

examples.quote: Rapid technological advances in artificial intelligence are transforming societies by changing the way people learn, work and live together.

proposals.label: AI widening North-South digital divide
proposals.definition: AI's evolution risks widening the digital divide between the global South and North, with calls on the UN to remove barriers to Africa's digital economy.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages warning that AI deepens the North-South divide or demanding removal of barriers (costs, IP rights) for developing regions.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages about crypto regulation or generic finance without a divide framing.
proposals.boundary_cases: Continuation passages listing digital-economy barriers without naming AI are coded here only when they continue an explicit AI-divide argument.

examples.quote: With the evolution of artificial intelligence, that divide risks becoming wider still.
eliminating barriers to the digital economy in Africa, such as the high costs of Internet services and intellectual property rights

proposals.label: Unregulated new technologies enabling crime
proposals.definition: New technologies such as cryptocurrency, when unregulated, facilitate crime, extremism and trafficking, motivating common global standards; AI is not named directly.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages on regulating emerging technologies against crime and instability where AI is part of the surrounding discussion.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages specifically about AI misuse (AI_CYBER_SECURITY).
proposals.boundary_cases: This is adjacent to AI discussion; classifiers should not treat crypto regulation alone as AI discourse.

examples.quote: new technologies, when not properly regulated, can facilitate organized crime, violent extremism and human trafficking

proposals.label: AI as neutral tool, rejecting paranoia
proposals.definition: AI is framed as a neutral dual-use tool whose effect depends on users, with anxiety attributed to distrust and a refusal to surrender to paranoia.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages rejecting AI alarmism and framing AI as a neutral tool usable for war or for development.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages that primarily warn of AI dangers.
proposals.boundary_cases: Balanced opportunity/risk statements without rejecting fear are AI_OPPORTUNITY_RISK_DUALITY.

examples.quote: we refuse to surrender our technological future to paranoia
We can deploy artificial intelligence to wage war or use it to transform healthcare, education, agriculture, governance, and economic productivity.

proposals.label: National digital investment and youth AI
proposals.definition: Speaker cites national investment in digital infrastructure, research and technology ownership and invites support for young people to direct AI.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages on national AI-enabling investments and youth AI talent.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude global governance calls.
proposals.boundary_cases: Youth invitation may also be coded AI_YOUTH_EDUCATION.

examples.quote: We invite the world to augment resourceful and enterprising young people to direct AI towards humanity's advancement rather than its destruction.

proposals.label: Fourth Industrial Revolution opportunities for youth
proposals.definition: AI and automation discussed in terms of youth prospects, skills and job certainty, with hope that technology becomes opportunity rather than threat for young people.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages linking AI/robotics to youth employment, skills or empowerment.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude generic development-access passages without a youth focus.
proposals.boundary_cases: Job-certainty concerns for youth also fit AI_ECONOMY_LABOR.

examples.quote: A future characterized by the rapid advancement of technology, advanced robotics, artificial intelligence and mechanization should present more opportunities, rather than problems, for our youth

proposals.label: Technology transfer and skills for developing countries
proposals.definition: Calls for technology transfer, adoption, skills development and collaboration so developing countries are not left behind in the AI/digital revolution.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages demanding technology transfer, skills or enabling environments for developing countries.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages only describing AI's transformation without calls to action.
